alalea.t: Alalea, CBAM and Turkish ETS guide

GBR.note: UK carbon border tax from 2027; linking with the EU system under negotiation.

NOR.note: In the EU emissions trading system through the European Economic Area.

ISL.note: In the EU emissions trading system through the European Economic Area.

CHE.instrument: Swiss ETS, linked to the EU
CHE.note: Linked to the EU system, so prices track the EU price.

CHN.note: Free, intensity-based allowances; each firm's surplus or shortfall capped at ±3%.

JPN.note: Baseline-and-credit; electric-furnace steel gets benchmarked free allocation.

CAN.price_text: C$95 headline (~€62); Alberta credits trade near C$18
CAN.note: Only emissions above an output-based limit pay; the federal benchmark is under review in 2026.

TWN.price_text: NT$300 per tonne (~€8.5); most plants pay NT$50–100
TWN.note: First payments for 2025 emissions in June 2026; steel paid about 8% of the total.

ZAF.note: Headline rate; allowances reduce what emitters actually pay.

AUS.note: Large emitters must stay under falling baselines or buy credits.

VNM.note: 25 steel plants covered; quotas about 4% below projected emissions.

IND.note: 255 steel units must meet emission-intensity targets from FY2026-27.

TUR.note: Steel is one of five pilot sectors.

CZE.note: Steel still receives most allowances for free; they are phased out as CBAM phases in (2026–2034).
CZE.trade: Inside the EU safeguard: 50% duty on imports above quota since Jul 2026; CBAM on imports from outside the EU.
